Fluorine is highly electronegative and can influence the reactivity of compounds significantly. Typically, the addition of fluorine atoms to organic molecules affects their chemical properties, such as stability and reactivity.

Fluorine, being highly electronegative, often decreases the reactivity of organic compounds by making the carbon-fluorine bond very strong and resistant to cleavage. This generally makes fluorinated compounds less reactive compared to their unfluorinated analogs.
